blockers.where: Prerequisites — "under **Settings access** on the **Account** tab of a user's permission set"
blockers.problem: The phrase "a user's permission set" is a console term with no backing fact in the Dossier, which records the permission's location only as "Account tab > Settings access" in the KB user-permissions guide.
blockers.suggestion: Drop the unbacked term and bridge with generic wording, e.g. "under **Settings access** on the **Account** tab when editing a user's permissions", so the location asserts only what the Dossier records.

blockers.problem: "Search, read, and manage HubSpot CRM records, engagements, and marketing content" asserts write access to marketing content, but the Dossier ({#content-write-limits}) records campaigns, website pages, blog posts, and marketing events as read-only, with landing pages the sole writable exception.
blockers.suggestion: Reword so "manage" covers only writable objects, e.g. "Search, read, and manage HubSpot CRM records and activities, and read marketing content, through the hosted HubSpot MCP server."

nits.problem: The term "engagements" appears nowhere in the Dossier, which names these objects "Activities: calls, emails, meetings, notes, and tasks."
nits.suggestion: Use "activities" in the summary to match the Dossier's terminology (this resolves together with the summary reword in the previous finding).

nits.where: setup.md#scopes-are-automatic — "Available scopes are determined automatically by two factors: the tools available in the MCP server at the time of installation, and the permissions the user chooses to grant during installation."
nits.problem: The gotcha teaches OAuth scope mechanics to a persona the file says does not know the word "scope" and must not be taught it — explanation the work does not require.
nits.suggestion: Lead with the practical fact in plain words and drop the mechanics, e.g.: "There is no permissions step anywhere in the MCP auth app flow — nothing is missing. What each user can access is set automatically when they connect, and is always capped by their own HubSpot permissions: users can only view and modify records they already have access to. Connecting never widens what an individual user can see or edit." Keep the anchor ID unchanged.

nits.where: setup.md#create-mcp-auth-app — "There is no scopes or permissions section — nothing is missing; access is determined automatically when each user connects"
nits.problem: The dialog note uses the OAuth term "scopes", which the persona explicitly does not know; "permissions section" alone carries the meaning.
nits.suggestion: Reword to "There is no permissions section — nothing is missing; what each user can access is set automatically when they connect (see ...)".

nits.where: setup.md#scope-updates-require-reinstall — "users who have already installed the app need to re-install it to grant the new scopes"
nits.problem: The guide's own framing throughout is that users "connect" from the Speakeasy AI Control Plane, but this gotcha switches to the provider's "install / re-install" vocabulary without bridging, so a literal reader cannot tell what action "re-install" maps to until the following example sentence.
nits.suggestion: Bridge the vocabulary at first use, e.g. "users who have already connected need to reconnect (HubSpot calls this re-installing the app) to grant the new access" — and prefer connect/reconnect in the heading text and body while keeping the anchor ID {#scope-updates-require-reinstall} unchanged.

nits.where: setup.md#keyword-search-only — "The MCP server is based on the CRM search API, which currently does not include vector search capabilities."
nits.problem: The gotcha opens with implementation detail ("CRM search API", "vector search capabilities") the persona does not need; only the second sentence states the practical behavior.
nits.suggestion: Lead with the practical sentence and subordinate or cut the implementation detail, e.g.: "Searches match keywords and property filters, not meaning — a search for 'unhappy customers' will not find tickets that never use those words. Set expectations with your users accordingly."

nits.where: setup.md#create-mcp-auth-app, step 4: "Add a **Description** and an **Icon** if you want them; both are optional."
nits.problem: The step performs two distinct actions (filling the Description field and the Icon field) inside one numbered step, where the persona's formatting rule calls for one action per numbered step.
nits.suggestion: Split into two steps, e.g. "4. Add a **Description** if you want one; it's optional." and "5. Add an **Icon** if you want one; it's optional." (renumbering the following **Create** step to 6).

nits.where: #copy-client-credentials — "if you navigate away before copying them, open the app again and copy them from there"
nits.problem: The recovery path never names the route back to the app, so a literal reader who has navigated away must guess how to reopen the details page.
nits.suggestion: Name the route in the recovery sentence: "return to **Development** > **MCP Auth Apps** in the left sidebar and select the app to reopen its details page" — the navigation is already documented in the Dossier's #open-mcp-auth-apps entry.

nits.where: Prerequisites — "if **Development** is missing from your navigation bar, that permission is the first thing to check"
nits.problem: A reader whose Developer tools access checks out but still sees no Development entry dead-ends with no next move, even though the Dossier records a second (conflicted, possibly stale) cause — the overview page's "new HubSpot Developer Platform" prerequisite.
nits.suggestion: Add one hedged fallback sentence after the permission note, e.g.: "If the permission is in place and **Development** still does not appear, ask HubSpot support whether your account is on the new HubSpot Developer Platform — one HubSpot page lists it as a requirement, though newer documentation says the server is available to all accounts."
